newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-PIERCE BEATS INJURED MARTINEZ IN ITALIAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE BEATS INJURED MARTINEZ IN ITALIAN FINAL.

text.p: France's Mary Pierce won the women's Italian Open for the first time on Sunday and ended an injured Conchita Martinez's record run of four consecutive titles.

The third-seeded Spaniard, undefeated on the Rome clay courts since the 1991 semifinals -- she did not compete in 1992 -- and who had not dropped a set on the way to the final, crashed to the 10th seed 6-4 6-0.
The 1994 Wimbledon champion said later she had suffered from a neck injury from the first set.
Martinez had problems with glare from objects in the crowd glinting in bright sunshine on her serve in the fourth game of the first set.
But the difficulties became more painful in the fifth game when she had a three-minute injury break.
"I had a problem with my neck," she said, adding it was a recurrence of a two-year old injury.
The Spaniard stayed with Pierce in the first set, breaking her, after treatment, for a 3-2 lead.
Pierce then broke straight back, held serve and broke again to lead 5-3. Martinez narrowed to 5-4 but was unable to hold her serve and handed Pierce the opening set with a ground stroke into the net.
It was one-way in the second set, with Martinez tossing her racket aside in the second game and selecting another, as Pierce took an immediate break.
The Frenchwoman romped away with it and a thumped backhand return with Martinez serving at 0-5, 0-40 gave her victory after one hour and 20 minutes.
